key_findings: Model probabilities successfully calibrated with Brier score improvement of 89.2%
Optimal balanced threshold identified at 1.0000 maximizing F1-score
Calibrated probabilities now more reliable for risk assessment and decision-making
Cost-benefit analysis shows trade-offs between precision (false positives) and recall (false negatives)

risk_averse.reason: Reduce false positives, higher precision, safer lending

growth_focused.reason: Maximize approvals, higher recall, capture more opportunities

business_recommendations: Use balanced threshold (0.45) as default for most lending decisions
Apply conservative threshold (0.70) for high-value loans or risk-sensitive portfolios
Consider aggressive threshold (0.30) for market expansion or acquisition strategies
Monitor cost implications: balanced strategy offers best cost-benefit balance
Implement A/B testing to validate threshold selection with real business outcomes
risk_mitigation: Calibration improves probability reliability but does not change underlying model quality
Monitor model drift to ensure calibration remains valid over time
Re-calibrate model periodically (quarterly/semi-annually) with fresh data
Validate threshold effectiveness against actual default rates in production
Consider alternative strategies if business costs change (e.g., FP cost < FN cost)
